key_idea: Just carry out the construction: incenter by side-weighted average, circumcenter by formula, second circle intersections of lines through I, then six line-line intersections.
sketch: Incenter I = (aA + bB + cC)/(a+b+c). Compute circumcenter O. For a vertex X on the circle with direction d = I - X, the second intersection is X + t*d with t = -2 (X-O).d / d.d, giving M, N, P. Intersect line NP with AB, AC to get E, F; MN with AC, BC to get G, H; MP with BC, AB to get J, K; print |EF| |FG| |GH| |HJ| |JK| |KE|. O(1) with doubles. Pitfalls: getting the hexagon vertex order right from a statement without its figure, and C may lie below the x-axis (orientation-independent formulas handle that).
